prologue.place.text: Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful
prologue.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

prologue.001.text: An old surgeon’s woodcut hangs by the hospice door: a man stuck with every blade, bolt and fang in the world — and standing.
prologue.001.speaker: Narrator
prologue.001.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 1 of 14.

prologue.002.text: Beneath it, in faded ink: “Here is the battlefield. Hold it.”
prologue.002.speaker: Narrator
prologue.002.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 2 of 14.

prologue.003.text: The Free City of Kessendorf. Winter, in the ninth year of the Long Muster.
prologue.003.speaker: Narrator
prologue.003.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 3 of 14.

prologue.004.text: The river has frozen twice. The pyres outside the east gate have not gone out since autumn.
prologue.004.speaker: Narrator
prologue.004.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 4 of 14.

prologue.005.text: So. You are the new sawbones the Guild sent me. Kreuzer, is it?
prologue.005.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.005.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 5 of 14.

prologue.006.text: Apothecary-surgeon, sworn at Weissburg. I have my letters, Master Haller—
prologue.006.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
prologue.006.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 6 of 14.

prologue.007.text: Letters. Letters don’t stop a man bleeding into the straw. Hands do. Show me your hands.
prologue.007.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.007.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 7 of 14.

prologue.008.text: …Steady enough. Why would a sworn Weissburg man take a charity bed in a city that burns its sick?
prologue.008.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.008.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 8 of 14.

prologue.009.text: Weissburg taught me the rules, Master. I came somewhere too poor to afford them.
prologue.009.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
prologue.009.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 9 of 14.

prologue.010.text: Hm. Sister! Our young doctor has arrived just in time for the Tuesday knife-fights.
prologue.010.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.010.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 10 of 14.

prologue.011.text: Sister Ilse, of the Merciful Order. I keep the instruments, the ledgers, and the Master’s temper.
prologue.011.speaker: Sister Ilse
prologue.011.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 11 of 14.

prologue.012.text: There’s a drover on the table already. Somebody at the Crooked Goose disagreed with his dice.
prologue.012.speaker: Sister Ilse
prologue.012.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 12 of 14.

prologue.013.text: Knife wounds. Simple work. I’ll watch.
prologue.013.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.013.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 13 of 14.

prologue.014.text: And Kreuzer — in this hospice we do not lose patients to simple work.
prologue.014.speaker: Master Haller
prologue.014.context: Story scene "prologue" (Kessendorf — the Hospice of Saint Ildra the Merciful), line 14 of 14.

op1-1.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op1-1.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op1-1.diagnosis.text: Knife wounds to the forearm and flank after a dice dispute. Moderate bleeding.
op1-1.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op1-1.p0.1.text: Two deep cuts. Take the Gut Thread and zig-zag across each wound to stitch it.
op1-1.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-1.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

op1-1.p0.2.text: Cross the wound again and again, moving along it. One smooth stroke earns the best marks.
op1-1.p0.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-1.p0.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

op1-1.p1.1.text: Blood’s pooled from the cuts. Hold the Leech-Pipe over it to draw it off.
op1-1.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-1.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

op1-1.p1.2.text: Next time, drain first — you can’t stitch through a pool of blood.
op1-1.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-1.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

op1-1.p2.1.text: Just nicks left. Brush Saint’s Salve over the small ones — no need for Gut Thread.
op1-1.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-1.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "A Tavern Knife" begins.

s1-2.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s1-2.001.text: The next morning the Watch arrives before the bread does.
s1-2.001.speaker: Narrator
s1-2.001.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 1 of 9.

s1-2.002.text: Make way! Make way, damn you! Surgeon! Where’s the surgeon?
s1-2.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
s1-2.002.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 2 of 9.

s1-2.003.text: Captain Mauer of the Watch. Lower your voice, Captain, this is a house of mercy.
s1-2.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-2.003.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 3 of 9.

s1-2.004.text: Twelve went out with the timber-road caravan. Twelve came back, eleven walking. Horned folk hit us at dawn.
s1-2.004.speaker: Captain Mauer
s1-2.004.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 4 of 9.

s1-2.005.text: Young Pieter took a shaft in the side. Twelve, Doctor. I’d like it to stay twelve.
s1-2.005.speaker: Captain Mauer
s1-2.005.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 5 of 9.

s1-2.006.text: Then put him down gently, Captain, and stop counting him among the dead.
s1-2.006.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-2.006.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 6 of 9.

s1-2.007.text: Horned-folk heads are barbed like fish-hooks. They cut a notch in their antlers for every one that sticks in a man.
s1-2.007.speaker: Master Haller
s1-2.007.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 7 of 9.

s1-2.008.text: Rip it straight out and you’ll take half his side with it. Free the barbs first, then pull. Cleanly.
s1-2.008.speaker: Master Haller
s1-2.008.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 8 of 9.

s1-2.009.text: Twelve. Say it with me, Doctor. Twelve.
s1-2.009.speaker: Captain Mauer
s1-2.009.context: Story scene "s1-2" (The Hospice — the next morning), line 9 of 9.

op1-2.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op1-2.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op1-2.diagnosis.text: Barbed arrow lodged in the left flank; crossbow bolt in the thigh. Raider ambush.
op1-2.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op1-2.p0.1.text: The arrow’s barbed. Lancet first — two nicks at the entry wound.
op1-2.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-2.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

op1-2.p0.2.text: Then seize it with the Tongs and pull it well clear.
op1-2.p0.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-2.p0.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

op1-2.p0.3.text: Then drain and stitch the wound it leaves.
op1-2.p0.3.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-2.p0.3.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

op1-2.p1.1.text: The bolt in his thigh has no barbs. Tongs, and pull it straight out.
op1-2.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-2.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

op1-2.p1.2.text: Quick, clean pulls earn the best marks.
op1-2.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-2.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 2 of "The Barbed Shaft" begins.

s1-3.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s1-3.001.text: Noon. A second sack of turnips arrives at the gate. The drover has told his friends about us.
s1-3.001.speaker: Narrator
s1-3.001.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 1 of 8.

s1-3.002.text: Doctor, the gunsmiths’ quarter. An apprentice was proving a new handgun barrel and it burst in his hands.
s1-3.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-3.002.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 2 of 8.

s1-3.003.text: Burns across the chest, lead driven under the skin — and a note from the Gunsmiths’ Guild pinned to his shirt.
s1-3.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-3.003.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 3 of 8.

s1-3.004.text: The Guild will pay for his care. Once we have paid the Guild’s fee for inspecting its own burst barrel.
s1-3.004.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-3.004.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 4 of 8.

s1-3.005.text: Naturally. In Kessendorf a man pays the Guild for the privilege of being shot by its work.
s1-3.005.speaker: Master Haller
s1-3.005.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 5 of 8.

s1-3.006.text: Then we send the Guild a bill for the lead we take out of him. Itemised, by the ounce.
s1-3.006.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-3.006.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 6 of 8.

s1-3.007.text: Powder burns. The black crust is dead meat: off with it before any salve, or it festers underneath.
s1-3.007.speaker: Master Haller
s1-3.007.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 7 of 8.

s1-3.008.text: The shot is deep. You’ll open him along the line I’ve inked. And if his pulse flags — the tincture.
s1-3.008.speaker: Master Haller
s1-3.008.context: Story scene "s1-3" (The Hospice — noon), line 8 of 8.

op1-3.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op1-3.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op1-3.diagnosis.text: Burst-barrel injury: powder burns across the chest, lead fragments embedded beneath the skin.
op1-3.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op1-3.p0.1.text: His pulse is weak already. Hold the Tincture to the flesh to steady him if need be.
op1-3.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-3.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

op1-3.p0.2.text: Burns first. Tongs to pluck the black eschar, then Saint’s Salve on the raw flesh.
op1-3.p0.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-3.p0.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

op1-3.p1.1.text: Now open him along the inked line with the Lancet. Start at the glowing end.
op1-3.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-3.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

op1-3.p2.1.text: There — the shot. Pull each ball out with the Tongs.
op1-3.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-3.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

op1-3.p3.1.text: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the Gut Thread.
op1-3.p3.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-3.p3.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Powder Burns" begins.

s1-4.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s1-4.001.text: Word travels fast in Kessendorf. By dusk, there is a queue at the hospice door.
s1-4.001.speaker: Narrator
s1-4.001.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 1 of 10.

s1-4.002.text: This one was found in the Tanners’ Rows. Swellings at the neck and groin. Fever. Maggots in an old sore.
s1-4.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-4.002.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 2 of 10.

s1-4.003.text: Matthis Kolb. Twenty years a tanner’s man. Write that, Sister, not “vagrant”. I had a trade before I had a fever.
s1-4.003.speaker: Matthis Kolb
s1-4.003.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 3 of 10.

s1-4.004.text: Matthis Kolb, tanner’s man. Written, and underlined.
s1-4.004.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-4.004.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 4 of 10.

s1-4.005.text: Buboes, and a rotting sore. He’s slept in the Rows among the hides. Burn the grubs, Kreuzer — not the man.
s1-4.005.speaker: Master Haller
s1-4.005.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 5 of 10.

s1-4.006.text: Nobody hears the door. There is simply a man in black standing in the ward, where a moment ago there was not.
s1-4.006.speaker: Narrator
s1-4.006.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 6 of 10.

s1-4.007.text: A plague case. In the city. How very interesting.
s1-4.007.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-4.007.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 7 of 10.

s1-4.008.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-4.008.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 8 of 10.

s1-4.009.text: Carry on, Doctor. I only wish to watch. Pestilence so often has a sponsor — and I hear the Kilnrows are coughing too.
s1-4.009.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-4.009.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 9 of 10.

s1-4.010.text: Then stand back from the table, Inquisitor. Whoever sponsors it, it isn’t particular whom it takes.
s1-4.010.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-4.010.context: Story scene "s1-4" (The Hospice — dusk), line 10 of 10.

op1-4.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op1-4.patient.text: Matthis Kolb, tanner’s man, Tanners’ Rows
op1-4.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op1-4.diagnosis.text: Plague buboes, spreading rot and an infested sore. High fever.
op1-4.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op1-4.p0.1.text: Lance each bubo with a single touch of the Lancet before it bursts.
op1-4.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-4.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

op1-4.p0.2.text: Then drain the pus and brush Saint’s Salve over it.
op1-4.p0.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-4.p0.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

op1-4.p1.1.text: Grubs in the sore! The Cautery Brand — hold it on each one until it stops moving.
op1-4.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-4.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

op1-4.p1.2.text: Don’t linger on bare flesh with the Cautery Brand.
op1-4.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-4.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

op1-4.p2.1.text: The rot’s spreading. Saint’s Salve on every patch — quickly, it creeps back.
op1-4.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-4.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Pestilent Humours" begins.

s1-5.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s1-5.001.text: Near midnight a carriage stops at the gate. Its door panel has been planed smooth where a crest should be — on purpose.
s1-5.001.speaker: Narrator
s1-5.001.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 1 of 8.

s1-5.002.text: The choir… they’re singing in me… make them stop singing…
s1-5.002.speaker: Page-boy Emmerich
s1-5.002.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 2 of 8.

s1-5.003.text: Doctor, look at his chest. Those marks — they’re moving. That one is an eye, with a stroke drawn through it.
s1-5.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-5.003.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 3 of 8.

s1-5.004.text: …That is no disease. Those are sigils. Someone has written on this boy.
s1-5.004.speaker: Master Haller
s1-5.004.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 4 of 8.

s1-5.005.text: Then we unwrite him. The brand, Sister. And more light.
s1-5.005.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-5.005.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 5 of 8.

s1-5.006.text: If something answers when you do — there is an old apothecary’s rite. The Litany of Stillness.
s1-5.006.speaker: Master Haller
s1-5.006.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 6 of 8.

s1-5.007.text: Draw the five-pointed star and still your heart. For a few breaths, the world will wait for you.
s1-5.007.speaker: Master Haller
s1-5.007.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 7 of 8.

s1-5.008.text: Do not do it where the Inquisitor can see. The Tribunal does not distinguish between a prayer and a spell.
s1-5.008.speaker: Master Haller
s1-5.008.context: Story scene "s1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 8 of 8.

op1-5.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op1-5.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op1-5.diagnosis.text: Unknown. Moving marks on the chest. Delirium. “The choir is singing in me.”
op1-5.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op1-5.p0.1.text: Those sigils are draining him. Trace every stroke with the Cautery Brand to sear them.
op1-5.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

op1-5.p1.1.text: Something is moving beneath the skin. We have to open him. The Lancet — along the line.
op1-5.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

op1-5.p2.1.text: Saints preserve us… what is that?
op1-5.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

op1-5.p2.2.text: Doctor — if ever there were a time for the Litany, it is now. Draw the star.
op1-5.p2.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p2.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

op1-5.p3.1.text: It’s gone. Tend the wounds it left.
op1-5.p3.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p3.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

op1-5.p4.1.text: Everything’s clear. Close the incision with the Gut Thread.
op1-5.p4.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op1-5.p4.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 5 of 5 of "The Hour of Matins" begins.

s1-end.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s1-end.001.text: The thing in the boy’s chest came apart like wet ash. The boy sleeps. He no longer hears singing.
s1-end.001.speaker: Narrator
s1-end.001.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 1 of 13.

s1-end.002.text: Doctor… after it broke, a word was left seared into the flesh. Matins. And beside it, fading: the struck-through eye.
s1-end.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
s1-end.002.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 2 of 13.

s1-end.003.text: The first of the canonical hours. The first prayer of the night.
s1-end.003.speaker: Master Haller
s1-end.003.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 3 of 13.

s1-end.004.text: A curse that lives and fights like a beast, and signs itself like a psalm. A Malison.
s1-end.004.speaker: Master Haller
s1-end.004.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 4 of 13.

s1-end.005.text: And if this was Matins… then somewhere, someone is already writing Lauds.
s1-end.005.speaker: Master Haller
s1-end.005.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 5 of 13.

s1-end.006.text: In the yard, the carriage without a crest pulls away before anyone thinks to ask whose it is.
s1-end.006.speaker: Narrator
s1-end.006.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 6 of 13.

s1-end.007.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-end.007.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 7 of 13.

s1-end.008.text: Tell me — at the end, your hands moved so very quickly. Almost as if time itself were… obliging you.
s1-end.008.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-end.008.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 8 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s1-end.009.text: Practice, Inquisitor. And the grace of Saint Ildra.
s1-end.009.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-end.009.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 9 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s1-end.010.text: Of course. The grace of the Saint. I shall pray on it.
s1-end.010.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-end.010.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 10 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s1-end.011.text: I watched every stroke. No tricks, no prayers. Only a surgeon, working. I find it almost disappointing.
s1-end.011.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s1-end.011.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 11 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

s1-end.012.text: Surgery usually is, Inquisitor. That is how you know it worked.
s1-end.012.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s1-end.012.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 12 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

s1-end.013.text: END OF CHAPTER I — THE HOUR OF MATINS
s1-end.013.speaker: Narrator
s1-end.013.context: Story scene "s1-end" (The Hospice — before dawn), line 13 of 13.

s2-1.place.text: The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf
s2-1.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-1.001.text: CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
s2-1.001.speaker: Narrator
s2-1.001.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 1 of 11.

s2-1.002.speaker: Narrator
s2-1.002.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 2 of 11.

s2-1.003.text: A week after the page-boy, a writ arrives under the Watch’s seal: the hospice’s surgeon is requisitioned for the muster.
s2-1.003.speaker: Narrator
s2-1.003.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 3 of 11.

s2-1.004.text: Don’t look at me like that, Doctor. The Inquisitor dines with the Burgomaster on Thursdays. On Fridays, the Burgomaster signs things.
s2-1.004.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-1.004.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 4 of 11.

s2-1.005.text: So Stroh can watch you somewhere with fewer witnesses.
s2-1.005.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-1.005.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 5 of 11.

s2-1.006.text: Fewer? Forty men in this camp, Sister. Forty witnesses. Forty-one with the cook, and I don’t count the cook.
s2-1.006.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-1.006.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 6 of 11.

s2-1.007.text: You count everyone, Captain. You counted the mules.
s2-1.007.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-1.007.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 7 of 11.

s2-1.008.text: The mules keep better order. We clear the Grauwald of raiders before the spring caravans. Two scouts came back from the barrow-fields.
s2-1.008.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-1.008.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 8 of 11.

s2-1.009.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-1.009.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 9 of 11.

s2-1.010.text: A gravehound. Claw rakes across his back — and it has left its teeth in him.
s2-1.010.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-1.010.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 10 of 11.

s2-1.011.text: Corpse-eaters carry a venom in their spit. Tomas, isn’t it? Look at me, Tomas. You’ll keep the arm.
s2-1.011.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-1.011.context: Story scene "s2-1" (The Timber Road — the Watch’s muster camp, three leagues east of Kessendorf), line 11 of 11.

op2-1.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op2-1.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op2-1.diagnosis.text: Mauled by a corpse-eating hound. Claw rakes across the back, fangs lodged in the shoulder, venom spreading from the bite.
op2-1.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op2-1.p0.1.text: The venom first — hold the Tincture on the bite until it takes.
op2-1.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-1.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

op2-1.p0.2.text: The longer it spreads, the harder it drags on him.
op2-1.p0.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-1.p0.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

op2-1.p1.1.text: Now the fangs. Tongs — pull each one clear.
op2-1.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-1.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

op2-1.p2.1.text: Claw rakes. Three deep lines — drain and stitch each.
op2-1.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-1.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "Gravehound" begins.

s2-2.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-2.001.text: Put me down, you long-legged oafs! I can walk! I can… mostly walk.
s2-2.001.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
s2-2.001.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 1 of 9.

s2-2.002.text: Dwarf prospector. Her crew was working a seam in the hills when it caved in.
s2-2.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-2.002.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 2 of 9.

s2-2.003.text: The rock went black, Doctor. Black as a wet eye, and it had a pulse. It sang when we struck it. Then it burst.
s2-2.003.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
s2-2.003.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 3 of 9.

s2-2.004.text: Mind her beard, Doctor. Every knot in it is tied for a debt.
s2-2.004.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-2.004.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 4 of 9.

s2-2.005.text: Nineteen knots. Nine are owed to me, ten I owe. If I die owing ten, my sons pay them, and my sons are idle.
s2-2.005.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
s2-2.005.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 5 of 9.

s2-2.006.text: There are shards under her skin I can’t see — but the flesh around them is spoiling.
s2-2.006.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-2.006.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 6 of 9.

s2-2.007.text: Master Haller sent his old Scrying Lens with me. He says you are to break anything else of his first.
s2-2.007.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-2.007.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 7 of 9.

s2-2.008.text: Dwarf hide’s thicker than yours, lad. You’ll want a strong arm on that thread.
s2-2.008.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
s2-2.008.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 8 of 9.

s2-2.009.text: Hold still, Mistress Flintvein, and I’ll owe you a knot.
s2-2.009.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-2.009.context: Story scene "s2-2" (The muster camp — afternoon), line 9 of 9.

op2-2.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op2-2.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op2-2.diagnosis.text: Cave-in at a hexstone seam. Shards driven beneath the skin, invisible to the eye. Surrounding flesh spoiling.
op2-2.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op2-2.p0.1.text: Rock splinters on the surface first. Tongs.
op2-2.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-2.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

op2-2.p1.1.text: Now — the Scrying Lens. Pass it slowly over the flesh; where something hides, it shimmers.
op2-2.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-2.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

op2-2.p1.2.text: Hold it still over the shimmer to bring the shard to light, then pull it.
op2-2.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-2.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

op2-2.p2.1.text: Clean up the spoiled flesh and any wounds left.
op2-2.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-2.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 3 of "The Black Seam" begins.

s2-3.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-3.001.text: Orsa sleeps in the supply wagon, snoring like a bellows. The sentries swear it keeps the wolves off.
s2-3.001.speaker: Narrator
s2-3.001.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 1 of 8.

s2-3.002.text: Elf forager. Went to check his snares by the old web-trees. We found him wrapped up like a midwinter ham.
s2-3.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-3.002.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 2 of 8.

s2-3.003.text: …the brood-mother… she kissed me… she was so gentle about it…
s2-3.003.speaker: Ilvaren
s2-3.003.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 3 of 8.

s2-3.004.text: Elf skin, Doctor — thin as vellum. It cuts at a breath and bleeds like a spring.
s2-3.004.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-3.004.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 4 of 8.

s2-3.005.text: The foresters call the great web-spinners brood-mothers. Venom, spreading fast. And these lumps… Saints. She laid in him.
s2-3.005.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-3.005.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 5 of 8.

s2-3.006.text: My lads won’t fetch water past the web-trees now. They say a brood-mother remembers every face that has seen her.
s2-3.006.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-3.006.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 6 of 8.

s2-3.007.text: Then fetch my water from somewhere she hasn’t looked, Captain. And more light.
s2-3.007.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-3.007.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 7 of 8.

s2-3.008.text: The sacs are swelling, Doctor. If they hatch on their own, they’ll scatter.
s2-3.008.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-3.008.context: Story scene "s2-3" (The muster camp — night), line 8 of 8.

op2-3.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op2-3.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op2-3.diagnosis.text: Web-spinner bite. Neurotoxic venom spreading from the neck; several egg sacs laid beneath the skin.
op2-3.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op2-3.p0.1.text: Venom from two bites. Tincture on each, quickly.
op2-3.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p1.1.text: The sacs — lance each with one touch, then sear the hatchlings with the Cautery Brand.
op2-3.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p1.2.text: Mind the ones that are close to hatching.
op2-3.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p2.1.text: Her brood-cluster — three sacs under one skin.
op2-3.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p2.2.text: Cut the membrane right around them with the Lancet first, or they’ll wake as one.
op2-3.p2.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p2.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p3.1.text: One more sac, deeper. Use the Scrying Lens to find it, then open it.
op2-3.p3.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p3.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

op2-3.p3.2.text: And he’s taken a fever-bubo from the bite — lance and cleanse it.
op2-3.p3.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-3.p3.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "Brood-Mother’s Kiss" begins.

s2-4.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-4.001.text: Doctor. I have brought you a gift.
s2-4.001.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.001.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 1 of 10.

s2-4.002.text: Two of the Inquisitor’s men drag a thin, grey-robed figure into the light. His chest is a lattice of glowing sigils.
s2-4.002.speaker: Narrator
s2-4.002.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 2 of 10.

s2-4.003.text: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir. We took him in the barrow-fields, singing to the dead. Something in the barrows sang back.
s2-4.003.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.003.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 3 of 10.

s2-4.004.text: The moment he began to confess, those marks ignited. He also swallowed something. His masters would rather he burned than spoke.
s2-4.004.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.004.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 4 of 10.

s2-4.005.text: You will keep him alive, Doctor — and awake. I have questions, and the dead are poor at answering them.
s2-4.005.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.005.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 5 of 10.

s2-4.006.text: …He’s dying, Doctor. Whatever else he is, he’s a patient.
s2-4.006.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-4.006.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 6 of 10.

s2-4.007.text: The cantor’s eyes find Kreuzer’s. Stroh waits, one glove already off.
s2-4.007.speaker: Narrator
s2-4.007.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 7 of 10. Choice prompt: the player then picks one of 2 replies (ids .o1–.o2).

s2-4.007.o1.text: I treat the man on my table, Inquisitor, not your witness. If he needs poppy for the pain, he has poppy.
s2-4.007.o1.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-4.007.o1.context: Reply 1 of 2 to the choice at s2-4.007; shown as a menu option, then in the backlog as Kreuzer's line. Sets `cantorMercy` = true.

s2-4.007.o2.text: You’ll have him alive and awake, Inquisitor. Keep your men out of my light.
s2-4.007.o2.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-4.007.o2.context: Reply 2 of 2 to the choice at s2-4.007; shown as a menu option, then in the backlog as Kreuzer's line. Sets `cantorMercy` = false.

s2-4.008.text: Poppy. So the Choir’s man sleeps soft while the city burns its sick. I shall remember whose mercy that was.
s2-4.008.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.008.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 8 of 10. Variant line: shown only if `cantorMercy` is set.

s2-4.009.text: Alive and awake. Good. We understand each other, Doctor — a rarer thing than you know.
s2-4.009.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-4.009.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 9 of 10. Variant line: shown only if `cantorMercy` is false.

s2-4.010.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-4.010.context: Story scene "s2-4" (The muster camp — before midnight), line 10 of 10.

op2-4.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op2-4.patient.text: A lay-cantor of the Hollow Choir
op2-4.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op2-4.diagnosis.text: Silence-sigils igniting across the chest (hexfire). Self-administered poison. Prisoner of the Ash Tribunal.
op2-4.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op2-4.p0.1.text: The poison he swallowed — Tincture, now, or he’s gone before we start.
op2-4.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

op2-4.p1.1.text: Those sigils are burning him from within. Sear each one out — every stroke.
op2-4.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

op2-4.p2.1.text: There — a knot of it round his throat. Every time he hums, it ties itself again.
op2-4.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

op2-4.p2.2.text: Burn it out between the verses.
op2-4.p2.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p2.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

op2-4.p3.1.text: The hexfire burns. Pluck the eschar, then Saint’s Salve on them.
op2-4.p3.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p3.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

op2-4.p4.1.text: Maggots in an old sore — the Tribunal’s cells are filthy. Cautery Brand.
op2-4.p4.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-4.p4.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 5 of 5 of "The Silenced Cantor" begins.

s2-5.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-5.001.text: Lauds… is sung at dawn… with the muster… under the banner…
s2-5.001.speaker: The cantor
s2-5.001.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 1 of 10.

s2-5.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-5.002.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 2 of 10.

s2-5.003.text: Across the camp, forty voices sing up the dawn. Beneath them, two more voices begin: one calling, one answering.
s2-5.003.speaker: Narrator
s2-5.003.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 3 of 10.

s2-5.004.text: Who keeps the watch before the sun?
s2-5.004.speaker: The first voice
s2-5.004.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 4 of 10.

s2-5.005.text: The one who wakes, and wakes alone.
s2-5.005.speaker: The answering voice
s2-5.005.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 5 of 10.

s2-5.006.text: Who sings the day when day is done?
s2-5.006.speaker: The first voice
s2-5.006.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 6 of 10.

s2-5.007.text: The one we answer, bone to bone.
s2-5.007.speaker: The answering voice
s2-5.007.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 7 of 10.

s2-5.008.text: The standard-bearer drops to his knees, the banner falling across him. The hymn falters. The two voices do not.
s2-5.008.speaker: Narrator
s2-5.008.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 8 of 10.

s2-5.009.text: Doctor! It’s Jorg — there are two of them in his chest, and each one answers the other!
s2-5.009.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-5.009.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 9 of 10.

s2-5.010.text: Clear a table. Sister — every instrument we have.
s2-5.010.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-5.010.context: Story scene "s2-5" (The muster camp — dawn), line 10 of 10.

op2-5.title.context: Operation title (briefing, HUD banner, results, theatre list).

op2-5.patient.context: Patient line on the chart and HUD.

op2-5.diagnosis.text: Collapsed during the dawn hymn. Something beneath the sternum is singing.
op2-5.diagnosis.context: Findings paragraph on the patient chart.

op2-5.p0.1.text: We have to open him — along the line, Doctor.
op2-5.p0.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-5.p0.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 1 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

op2-5.p1.1.text: A choir! Those lights are its Voices — hold the Cautery Brand on each as it circles.
op2-5.p1.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-5.p1.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

op2-5.p1.2.text: Silence all of them and its heart will be bare.
op2-5.p1.2.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-5.p1.2.context: Assistant callout when phase 2 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

op2-5.p2.1.text: It’s done. Tend what it left of him.
op2-5.p2.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-5.p2.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 3 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

op2-5.p3.1.text: Close him up. Gently — he has a banner to carry.
op2-5.p3.1.speaker: Sister Ilse
op2-5.p3.1.context: Assistant callout when phase 4 of 4 of "The Hour of Lauds" begins.

s2-end.place.context: Place and time caption at the top-left of the scene.

s2-end.001.text: The singing stops. The standard-bearer breathes. In the flesh over his heart, a single word: LAUDS.
s2-end.001.speaker: Narrator
s2-end.001.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 1 of 13.

s2-end.002.text: And beside it — Doctor, look. An eye with a stroke through it. The same mark the page-boy carried.
s2-end.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-end.002.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 2 of 13.

s2-end.003.text: Two of them now. Matins in the city, Lauds in my own camp. Someone is keeping time, Doctor.
s2-end.003.speaker: Captain Mauer
s2-end.003.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 3 of 13.

s2-end.004.text: Six more hours to the full Office. Prime. Terce. Sext. None. Vespers. Compline.
s2-end.004.speaker: Sister Ilse
s2-end.004.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 4 of 13.

s2-end.005.text: In the ward tent a wounded pikeman hums the dawn hymn in his sleep. Two notes. Then, from nowhere, the answer.
s2-end.005.speaker: Narrator
s2-end.005.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 5 of 13.

s2-end.006.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-end.006.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 6 of 13.

s2-end.007.text: When that thing screamed, every candle in this tent stopped flickering. The flames stood still. For eight heartbeats.
s2-end.007.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-end.007.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 7 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s2-end.008.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-end.008.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 8 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s2-end.009.text: …The morning air is very still, Inquisitor.
s2-end.009.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-end.009.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 9 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was spoken in the preceding operation.

s2-end.010.text: I watched your hands while that thing screamed. They shook, Doctor. For once.
s2-end.010.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-end.010.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 10 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

s2-end.011.text: It was a long night, Inquisitor.
s2-end.011.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
s2-end.011.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 11 of 13. Variant line: shown only if the Litany was NOT spoken in the preceding operation.

s2-end.012.text: We will speak at length, you and I. After Prime.
s2-end.012.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
s2-end.012.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 12 of 13.

s2-end.013.text: END OF CHAPTER II — THE HOUR OF LAUDS
s2-end.013.speaker: Narrator
s2-end.013.context: Story scene "s2-end" (The muster camp — morning), line 13 of 13.

a1-1.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1".

a1-1.001.text: The drover lives. He pays in turnips and a promise not to gamble again. He will break it by Friday.
a1-1.001.speaker: Narrator
a1-1.001.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 1 of 6.

a1-1.002.text: Clean. Quick. Hm. Don’t let it go to your head, Kreuzer. It was simple work.
a1-1.002.speaker: Master Haller
a1-1.002.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 2 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-1.003.text: Adequate. The Weissburg Guild would call that adequate. I call it Tuesday.
a1-1.003.speaker: Master Haller
a1-1.003.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 3 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-1.004.text: He’ll live. Eventually. I said simple work, Kreuzer. I did not say leisurely.
a1-1.004.speaker: Master Haller
a1-1.004.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 4 of 6. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-1.005.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a1-1.005.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 5 of 6.

a1-1.006.text: Under “fees, vegetable”. We have a column. It is the longest one in the ledger.
a1-1.006.speaker: Sister Ilse
a1-1.006.context: Aftermath scene after op1-1 "a1-1" (The Hospice — after the knife-work), line 6 of 6.

a1-2.place.text: The Hospice — after the barbed shaft
a1-2.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2".

a1-2.001.text: Pieter will keep his side, and his opinion of the horned folk.
a1-2.001.speaker: Narrator
a1-2.001.context: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 1 of 4.

a1-2.002.text: Twelve. Twelve walking. The Watch pays its debts, Doctor. Slowly, but it pays.
a1-2.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
a1-2.002.context: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 2 of 4.

a1-2.003.text: You nicked those barbs like a tailor. Where did Weissburg find the time to teach you that?
a1-2.003.speaker: Master Haller
a1-2.003.context: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-2.004.text: You tore him on the second barb. He will heal. He will also remember you.
a1-2.004.speaker: Master Haller
a1-2.004.context: Aftermath scene after op1-2 "a1-2" (The Hospice — after the barbed shaft), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-3.place.text: The Hospice — after the burst barrel
a1-3.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3".

a1-3.001.text: Anno keeps both hands. The Guild keeps its fee. Nobody keeps the barrel.
a1-3.001.speaker: Narrator
a1-3.001.context: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 1 of 4.

a1-3.002.text: His master called. He asked whether the lead we took out of the boy could be melted down again.
a1-3.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
a1-3.002.context: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 2 of 4.

a1-3.003.text: Tell him yes. Tell him it is the best-proven lead in Kessendorf.
a1-3.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a1-3.003.context: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 3 of 4.

a1-3.004.text: The boy will scar. Burns remember every minute you wasted, Kreuzer. So do I.
a1-3.004.speaker: Master Haller
a1-3.004.context: Aftermath scene after op1-3 "a1-3" (The Hospice — after the burst barrel), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a1-4.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4".

a1-4.001.text: Matthis Kolb sleeps in a clean bed for the first time in a year. He asks Ilse to read his name back to him, twice.
a1-4.001.speaker: Narrator
a1-4.001.context: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 1 of 4.

a1-4.002.text: Buboes in winter. The pestilence is early this year, Doctor. Or it was invited.
a1-4.002.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a1-4.002.context: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 2 of 4.

a1-4.003.text: Fevers don’t wait for invitations, Inquisitor.
a1-4.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a1-4.003.context: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 3 of 4.

a1-4.004.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a1-4.004.context: Aftermath scene after op1-4 "a1-4" (The Hospice — after dark), line 4 of 4.

a2-1.place.text: The muster camp — after the gravehound
a2-1.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1".

a2-1.001.text: The scout will limp, but he will limp home.
a2-1.001.speaker: Narrator
a2-1.001.context: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 1 of 3.

a2-1.002.text: Forty. Still forty. I am starting to like you, Doctor, and I don’t care for it.
a2-1.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
a2-1.002.context: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 2 of 3.

a2-1.003.text: Every tooth, and not a drop of venom left. Master Haller would pretend not to be impressed.
a2-1.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
a2-1.003.context: Aftermath scene after op2-1 "a2-1" (The muster camp — after the gravehound), line 3 of 3. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a2-2.place.text: The muster camp — the supply wagon
a2-2.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2".

a2-2.001.text: A strong arm after all. I shall name a mine for you, Doctor. The Kreuzer Deep.
a2-2.001.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
a2-2.001.context: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 1 of 4.

a2-2.002.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a2-2.002.context: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 2 of 4.

a2-2.003.text: It is not dug yet. It will probably be a bad one. The first ones always are.
a2-2.003.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
a2-2.003.context: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 3 of 4.

a2-2.004.text: Here. One knot, untied. You owe me nothing, and I owe you one.
a2-2.004.speaker: Orsa Flintvein
a2-2.004.context: Aftermath scene after op2-2 "a2-2" (The muster camp — the supply wagon), line 4 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a2-3.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3".

a2-3.001.text: Ilvaren wakes asking after his snares. The web-trees are left to the foresters, and to the fire.
a2-3.001.speaker: Narrator
a2-3.001.context: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 1 of 3.

a2-3.002.text: Forty, and a forager who will never set a snare again. My lads are calling you the spider-cutter.
a2-3.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
a2-3.002.context: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 2 of 3.

a2-3.003.text: Tell them I have been called worse by better men.
a2-3.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a2-3.003.context: Aftermath scene after op2-3 "a2-3" (The muster camp — after midnight), line 3 of 3.

a2-4.place.text: The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent
a2-4.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4".

a2-4.001.text: The cantor breathes. The sigils on his chest are ash. Stroh’s men stand at the tent flap and do not let the Doctor leave.
a2-4.001.speaker: Narrator
a2-4.001.context: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 1 of 3.

a2-4.002.text: He lives. Good. Now he can tell me who taught him to sing.
a2-4.002.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a2-4.002.context: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 2 of 3.

a2-4.003.text: He is a patient until he walks out of this tent, Inquisitor. Then he is yours. Not one hour sooner.
a2-4.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
a2-4.003.context: Aftermath scene after op2-4 "a2-4" (The muster camp — the Inquisitor’s tent), line 3 of 3.

a3-1.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1".

a3-1.001.text: Liesl wakes with a bandage like a crown and asks whether she may keep the bits of horn. Her mother says no. Kreuzer says yes.
a3-1.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-1.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 1 of 3.

a3-1.002.text: Two buds, cut clean. And two sigils seared away beneath them, where no certificate will mention them.
a3-1.002.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a3-1.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 2 of 3.

a3-1.003.text: The certificate mentions a natural growth, Inquisitor. I removed it.
a3-1.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a3-1.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-1 "a3-1" (The hospice — the examining room), line 3 of 3.

a3-2.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2".

a3-2.001.text: Kaspar’s doublet goes into a basin, a scrap at a time. Ilse counts them twice and matches every thread to the hole it came from.
a3-2.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-2.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 1 of 4.

a3-2.002.text: Every scrap, Doctor. He’ll not be burning by Vespers. He may be dancing by Terce.
a3-2.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
a3-2.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 2 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a3-2.003.text: I pray that was every scrap. We’ll know by Vespers, if he’s burning.
a3-2.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
a3-2.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid or low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a3-2.004.text: Next! Three off the mill cart, Doctor, and the cart’s coming back for more.
a3-2.004.speaker: Captain Mauer
a3-2.004.context: Aftermath scene after op3-2 "a3-2" (The hospice — the steps), line 4 of 4.

a3-3.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3".

a3-3.001.text: Ute Brandt goes home lighter by a quarter-pound of lead, which Ilse weighs, wraps, and labels for the Founders’ Guild.
a3-3.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-3.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 1 of 3.

a3-3.002.text: Put it in the privy basket. The Guild may send a clerk to collect its property.
a3-3.002.speaker: Master Haller
a3-3.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 2 of 3.

a3-3.003.text: I have already written the receipt, Master. “One quarter-pound of lead, lightly used.”
a3-3.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
a3-3.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-3 "a3-3" (The hospice — night), line 3 of 3.

a3-4.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4".

a3-4.001.text: Jannik, Old Rudi and Wenzel lie in a row on the hospice steps, wrapped in one blanket, arguing about whose fault the magazine was.
a3-4.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-4.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 1 of 3.

a3-4.002.text: Three off the table and three still talking. That’s a good count for the Kilnrows.
a3-4.002.speaker: Captain Mauer
a3-4.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 2 of 3.

a3-4.003.text: Keep them talking, Captain. A man complaining is a man breathing.
a3-4.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a3-4.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-4 "a3-4" (The hospice — the steps, evening), line 3 of 3.

a3-5.place.text: The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut
a3-5.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5".

a3-5.001.text: Berthold wakes to find his leg gone and his cart-horse tethered outside the window, which he says is the right way round.
a3-5.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-5.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 1 of 3.

a3-5.002.text: A peg and a cushion, you said. I’ll hold you to the cushion, Doctor.
a3-5.002.speaker: Berthold
a3-5.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 2 of 3.

a3-5.003.text: The council has sent a clerk to ask who will pay for the bridge-chain he bent. I sent the clerk away. Twice.
a3-5.003.speaker: Captain Mauer
a3-5.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-5 "a3-5" (The Iron Bridge — the Watch hut), line 3 of 3.

a3-6.place.text: The quarantine side — the Penny Stair
a3-6.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6".

a3-6.001.text: Forty-one worms, whole, in a jar. Gottfried the pie-man is asked to look at it, and does, and is quiet for a while.
a3-6.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-6.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 1 of 3.

a3-6.002.text: Eel. They told me it was eel.
a3-6.002.speaker: Gottfried, pie-man
a3-6.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 2 of 3.

a3-6.003.text: Then someone owes Frieda an apology, Gottfried, and you owe the city a new recipe.
a3-6.003.speaker: Sister Ilse
a3-6.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-6 "a3-6" (The quarantine side — the Penny Stair), line 3 of 3.

a3-7.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7".

a3-7.001.text: Mother Agathe of the Grey Beguines sits up at the fourth bell and demands her beads, her boots, and a list of the other sick.
a3-7.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-7.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7" (The quarantine ward — before dawn), line 1 of 2.

a3-7.002.text: You lance like a Beguine, boy. That is the highest praise I have. Now go and do it to someone else.
a3-7.002.speaker: Mother Agathe
a3-7.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-7 "a3-7" (The quarantine ward — before dawn), line 2 of 2.

a3-8.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8".

a3-8.001.text: Brother Ansgar sleeps face-down with his hands open. The nails are in a bowl beside him. He has not asked for them back.
a3-8.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-8.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 1 of 3.

a3-8.002.text: He asked me whether a debt can be paid by someone else. I told him the Order thinks so. I hope it does.
a3-8.002.speaker: Sister Ilse
a3-8.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 2 of 3.

a3-8.003.text: Let him sleep, Sister. We can argue theology when his back has closed.
a3-8.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a3-8.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-8 "a3-8" (The quarantine ward — dawn), line 3 of 3.

a3-10.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10".

a3-10.001.text: The Registrar’s skin is clean. The roll of the dead is the right length again, and every name on it had a family to miss it.
a3-10.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-10.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 1 of 4.

a3-10.002.text: I read the names of strangers, Doctor. People who had not died. Did they… will they?
a3-10.002.speaker: Registrar Tallert
a3-10.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 2 of 4.

a3-10.003.text: Not from anything you read, Registrar. Go home. Read something with a happy ending.
a3-10.003.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a3-10.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 3 of 4.

a3-10.004.text: The names stopped when you touched him, Doctor. I noticed. I notice things.
a3-10.004.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a3-10.004.context: Aftermath scene after op3-10 "a3-10" (The Hall of Records — morning), line 4 of 4.

a3-9.place.context: Place caption of aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9".

a3-9.001.text: The Inquisitor sits with a cloth to his jaw and his tooth in a twist of paper, which he pockets like evidence.
a3-9.001.speaker: Narrator
a3-9.001.context: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 1 of 4.

a3-9.002.text: That was… gentle, Doctor. I had been told barbers enjoy it. I shall have to revise the Tribunal’s view of your trade.
a3-9.002.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a3-9.002.context: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 2 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was high (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a3-9.003.text: The root came out in two pieces. So, very nearly, did I. We shall say no more of it.
a3-9.003.speaker: Inquisitor Stroh
a3-9.003.context: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 3 of 4. Variant line: shown only if the preceding operation's rank was mid or low (high = XS/S, mid = A/B, low = C).

a3-9.004.text: Rinse with salt, Inquisitor. And ask your questions in daylight.
a3-9.004.speaker: Dr. Kreuzer
a3-9.004.context: Aftermath scene after op3-9 "a3-9" (The hospice — past midnight), line 4 of 4.

f1-1.place.text: The Hospice — the table goes still
f1-1.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-1".

f1-1.001.text: Simple work, Kreuzer. Wash your hands. Look at the wounds again. Then do it properly.
f1-1.001.speaker: Master Haller
f1-1.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-1" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

f1-2.place.text: The Hospice — the table goes still
f1-2.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2".

f1-2.001.speaker: Captain Mauer
f1-2.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 2.

f1-2.002.text: Free the barbs before you pull, not after. Again, Kreuzer. He is not yet cold, and neither are you.
f1-2.002.speaker: Master Haller
f1-2.002.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-2" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 2 of 2.

f1-3.place.text: The Hospice — the table goes still
f1-3.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-3".

f1-3.001.text: His pulse was fading, Doctor, and we let it fade. The tincture is there to be used.
f1-3.001.speaker: Sister Ilse
f1-3.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-3" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

f1-4.place.text: The Hospice — the table goes still
f1-4.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-4 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-4".

f1-4.001.text: I wrote his name down. I will not write it in the other ledger. Not tonight. Again, Doctor.
f1-4.001.speaker: Sister Ilse
f1-4.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-4 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-4" (The Hospice — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

f1-5.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op1-5 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-5".

f1-5.001.text: It fights, Kreuzer. It is meant to. Brand it only when it opens its eye — and remember the star.
f1-5.001.speaker: Master Haller
f1-5.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op1-5 dies, before the retry prompt "f1-5" (The Hospice — the small hours), line 1 of 1.

f2-1.place.text: The muster camp — the table goes still
f2-1.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-1".

f2-1.001.text: Thirty-nine. …No. Not yet. Doctor, do it again. I’m not writing that number down.
f2-1.001.speaker: Captain Mauer
f2-1.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op2-1 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-1" (The muster camp — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

f2-2.place.text: The muster camp — the table goes still
f2-2.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-2".

f2-2.001.text: The shards we could not see were the ones that killed her. Slower with the lens, Doctor.
f2-2.001.speaker: Sister Ilse
f2-2.001.context: Failure scene when the patient of op2-2 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-2" (The muster camp — the table goes still), line 1 of 1.

f2-3.place.text: The muster camp — the table goes still
f2-3.place.context: Place caption of failure scene when the patient of op2-3 dies, before the retry prompt "f2-3".

f2-3.001.text: The sacs hatched before we lanced them. We know which ones now. Again.
f2-3.001.speaker: Sister Ilse

tutorial.tongs.text: Tongs {TOOL_TONGS}: hold {USE} on the object and drag it well clear of the body.

tutorial.tincture.text: Tincture {TOOL_TINCTURE}: hold {USE} on the body to steady a failing pulse.
tutorial.tincture.context: Tutorial prompt, first shown in op1-3. Keep {TOKENS} verbatim: they become key/button glyphs. Imperative, one instruction.

footnote.op1-1.text: Jost the drover swore off dice for good. He broke the promise by Friday, and the stitches held anyway.
footnote.op1-1.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-1, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op1-2.text: Pieter kept the arrowhead on a cord round his neck and told the militia it was from a duel.
footnote.op1-2.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-2, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op1-3.text: Anno went back to the gunsmith’s bench and now stands to the side of every barrel he proves.
footnote.op1-3.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-3, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op1-4.text: Matthis Kolb returned to the Tanners’ Rows, and would speak of the buboes to no one but the hospice cat.
footnote.op1-4.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-4, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op1-5.text: Emmerich no longer hears the singing. He sleeps with a candle lit, and nobody at the hospice has the heart to stop him.
footnote.op1-5.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op1-5, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op2-1.text: Tomas kept the arm, and learned to throw left-handed anyway, in case.
footnote.op2-1.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-1, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op2-2.text: Orsa Flintvein walked back to her diggings with the shards in a lead box and a promise to return the favour.
footnote.op2-2.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-2, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op2-3.text: Ilvaren went home to the Grauwald and planted the spider’s thicket with nettles.
footnote.op2-3.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-3, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op2-4.text: The lay-cantor’s hymn is written in the Inquisitor’s ledger, in a hand that pressed hard enough to tear the page.
footnote.op2-4.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-4, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

footnote.op2-5.text: Jorg carried the standard again at the next muster. He hums, now, without noticing, and stops when anyone looks.
footnote.op2-5.context: "Where are they now" line for the patient of op2-5, read after the chapter ends. Narration; wry, not cruel.

teaser-3.001.text: Foundry smoke lies so thick over the Kilnrows that the lamplighters go out at noon.
teaser-3.001.speaker: Narrator
teaser-3.001.context: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 1 of 6.

teaser-3.002.text: At dusk the river bridges are raised, and the Watch asks every child at the gate to show its forehead.
teaser-3.002.speaker: Narrator
teaser-3.002.context: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 2 of 6.

teaser-3.003.text: The Guild will put your licence to the vote, boy. I stood in that hall once before. I can stand in it again.
teaser-3.003.speaker: Master Haller
teaser-3.003.context: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 3 of 6.

teaser-3.004.text: Doctor, there is a girl at the door with two nubs of horn in her hair, and her mother is praying.

teaser-3.004.context: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 4 of 6.

teaser-3.005.text: On the steps of the Hall of Records, a registrar reads the roll of the dead aloud, and the names keep coming.
teaser-3.005.speaker: Narrator
teaser-3.005.context: Chapter III teaser read after the demo end card "teaser-3" (Next — Chapter III: Prime and Terce), line 5 of 6.

teaser-3.006.text: I said we would speak after Prime, Doctor. It is nearly after Prime.
